subject: Encord <> CleanConnect - catch up
text:
Hi [NAME],

Congrats on the EPA approval for your LeakFinder system! My colleague [SENDER]
mentioned you guys connected a while back, and I wanted to introduce
myself.

I know you mentioned that you were using CVAT and have an annotation team. With
your recent growth, I was just curious if there have been any new
challenges around your data pipeline/ maintaining model accuracy for
detecting leaks in complex environments.

models) so engineering can focus on improving model performance.

Would you be open to a quick 20-minute chat to revisit? I'm flexible
Tuesday to Thursday next week.

text:
Hi [NAME],

Congrats on the Preem partnership. Love seeing [COMPANY] pushing
sustainability in industrial AI (and making the Earth greener!)

The reason for my outreach is to chat about how computer vision plays into
[COMPANY]'s AI roadmap. If you're anything like our clients in energy and
industrials, you see challenges as datasets grow (sensor, video, 3D),
managing complex annotation pipelines starts slowing model development and
stretching engineering resources.

That's where we've been helping teams like Baker Hughes and Buzz Solutions,
to streamline annotation for high-volume, complex datasets so they can
boost predictive accuracy and get models into production faster. Curious to
see how you are currently handling training data as you scale.

Do you have time over the next week or two to visit more? Let me know what
works for you, and I'll send a calendar invite accordingly.

subject: CVPR + Google Research Scholar Award + Encord
text:
Hi [NAME],

We've not yet been introduced. I'm [SENDER] and run industrial partnerships at
Encord. I came across your profile while researching CVPR and noticed your
Google Research Scholar Award. Really impressive to see your academic
achievements translating into impactful commercial success at [COMPANY]. It's
rare to see industrial AI simultaneously drive profitability and
sustainability.

From what I understand, [COMPANY] has been sensor-driven in its optimization
models. I'm curious whether you see a role for computer vision alongside
that work. Leaders we support (Baker Hughes, Zeitview, Buzz Solutions)
often combine CV inspection (e.g. defect detection, leak monitoring, asset
condition tracking, etc) with process optimization to create a fuller
operational picture.

That's where Encord comes in: our platform streamlines the data side of CV
development (curation, annotation, QA, model evaluation) so teams can
iterate faster while retaining full control of their pipelines. Not sure
how familiar you are with Encord: we're a data development platform built
for advanced CV and multimodal AI (image, video, 3D, point cloud). We're ~5
years old with 100+ employees and raised $50M+ in funding.

Would you be open to a short chat to compare notes on scaling industrial AI
and where visual inspection could (or might not) fit into [COMPANY]'s roadmap?

I'd be happy to send an invite along accordingly.
